headline: Connecting internal or personal accounts works immediately, but onboarding external enterprise users practically requires Microsoft Publisher Verification which takes 3 to 5 business days.
summary: Microsoft Outlook uses OAuth 2.0 via Microsoft Graph and Microsoft Entra ID. Registering an application is free and self-service in the Entra ID portal. Personal Microsoft accounts and internal test users can consent immediately, though personal users will see an 'unverified' warning. For external enterprise users (B2B), Microsoft's default risk-based policies block end-user consent for unverified apps, making Publisher Verification effectively mandatory for production multi-tenant apps.

oauth.pkce: Supported and recommended for all clients; mandatory for Single Page Applications (SPAs) and public mobile/desktop clients.
oauth.refresh_tokens: Requires the 'offline_access' scope. Tokens have a rolling inactivity window of 90 days and a default maximum lifetime of until revoked.
oauth.redirect_uri_rules: Must use https:// scheme (except for localhost development), exact string matching is enforced (no wildcards or query parameters), case-sensitive, max length 256 characters.
oauth.scopes: User.Read, offline_access, Mail.Read, Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Send, Mail.ReadBasic

steps.title: Register App in Entra ID
steps.detail: Create the app registration in the Microsoft Entra admin center, selecting the appropriate multi-tenant supported account type.

steps.title: Configure Redirect URIs and Scopes
steps.detail: Add standard redirect URIs, generate client secrets, and configure delegated Microsoft Graph permissions (e.g., Mail.Read, User.Read).

steps.title: Set Publisher Branding
steps.detail: Configure the application's Privacy Statement URL, Terms of Service URL, and verified custom domain.

steps.title: Enroll in MAICPP
steps.detail: Enroll in the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program (MAICPP) and submit legal entity details for business vetting.

steps.title: Wait for Legal Vetting
steps.detail: Wait for Microsoft to complete the business identity vetting process in Partner Center.

steps.title: Link Partner ID to App
steps.detail: As an Entra ID Application Administrator and MPN Admin with MFA enabled, link the vetted Partner Global Account ID to the app registration.

requirements.text: An active Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program (MAICPP) account with an approved Partner Global Account (PGA) PartnerID.
A DNS-verified custom domain registered in Entra ID that exactly matches the legal entity's web domain vetted in Partner Center.
Configured Privacy Statement URL and Terms of Service URL in the app registration.

The administrator executing publisher verification must have MFA enabled and hold Application Administrator (or Cloud Application Administrator) in Entra ID and MPN Partner Admin (or Account Admin) in Partner Center.

gotchas.text: OpenID Connect discovery metadata is not published at the standard /common or /common/v2.0 endpoints.
Without Publisher Verification, external enterprise (Entra ID) users will see a 'Need admin approval' block by default due to Microsoft's risk-based step-up policies.
Application permissions (daemon or service-to-service access without a user present) always strictly require Tenant Administrator Consent, regardless of Publisher Verification.
Microsoft Graph enforces rate limits of 10,000 API requests per 10-minute period per app/mailbox pair.
Discrepancies between the legal entity names/addresses on official utility bills and the Partner Center profile can cause vetting delays or rejection.

permissions.action: Authenticate users, read basic profile, and maintain offline access
permissions.review_impact: End-users can self-consent, but B2B enterprise users will be blocked unless the app completes Publisher Verification.
End-users can self-consent as a delegated permission. Blocked for B2B users without Publisher Verification. As an Application permission, strictly requires Tenant Administrator Consent.

permissions.action: Send emails on behalf of the user
permissions.review_impact: End-users can self-consent. Blocked for B2B users without Publisher Verification.

permissions.action: Create, read, update, or delete emails
permissions.review_impact: End-users can self-consent. Blocked for B2B users without Publisher Verification.

blockers.issue: Users see a 'Need admin approval' screen and cannot connect their work/school accounts.
blockers.how_to_proceed: You must complete Publisher Verification in Microsoft Partner Center. Until then, a tenant administrator for that user's organization must explicitly grant tenant-wide consent to your app.

blockers.issue: Publisher Verification fails with error MPNAccountNotVetted.
blockers.how_to_proceed: Wait for Microsoft to finish checking your legal entity documents in Partner Center, or check the Partner Center portal to see if additional utility bills/business documents are requested.

blockers.issue: Publisher Verification fails with error MPNAccountNotFoundOrNoAccess.
blockers.how_to_proceed: Ensure you are using the Partner Global Account (PGA) ID, not a Location ID. Verify your signed-in user has MFA enabled, holds the Application Administrator role in Entra ID, and holds the MPN Partner Admin role in Partner Center.

agent_can: Register the application in Microsoft Entra ID and generate client credentials
Configure API permissions, redirect URIs, and token settings
Draft the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy required for branding
Test the authorization and token exchange flow using internal test accounts
you_must: Verify your DNS domain ownership in Entra ID
Create a Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program (MAICPP) account
Submit official legal documents (e.g., utility bills, incorporation docs) for business verification
Link your Partner Global Account ID to the Entra ID application with an MFA-enabled admin account

key_claims.text: Publisher verification is effectively mandatory for multi-tenant apps connecting commercial Microsoft 365 accounts due to risk-based step-up policies.
Microsoft Graph authorization endpoints are active, though OIDC discovery metadata is not published at the root /common paths.
Refresh tokens have a rolling inactivity window of 90 days and default to a maximum lifetime of 'until revoked'.
Publisher Verification is free and typical business vetting in Partner Center takes 3 to 5 business days.

open_questions: Exact processing time if legal documents are rejected and require manual appeal in Partner Center.
assumptions: Hands-on time is our estimate, not published by the provider.
The primary use case targets external B2B multi-tenant users, which necessitates Publisher Verification.
Review time is based on Microsoft's stated typical vetting times, though anecdotal evidence suggests it can take longer if document details do not match exactly.
